in_greek.name: Βικτωρίν
in_greek.long_meaning: Βικτωρίν είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από τη λατινική λέξη Victor, που σημαίνει 'νικητής' ή 'αυτός που κερδίζει'. Το όνομα συνδέεται με τη νίκη επί του κακού και την πνευματική νίκη που έρχεται μέσω της πίστης. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα Βικτωρίν συμβολίζει τη δύναμη και τη νίκη που δίνει ο Θεός στους πιστούς.

historical_references.reference: Saint Victorinus of Mariborus, also known as Victorinus of Pettau, was a bishop in the Roman Empire during the late 3rd and early 4th centuries. He is believed to have lived from around 270 to 304 AD and is considered one of the most important early Christian writers from the eastern part of the empire. He was born in Pannonia, a province of the Roman Empire in present-day Hungary, and is best known for his works 'De idolatria' and 'Ad Autolycum', which were influential in the early Christian debates against paganism.
historical_references.context: Early Christian writer and bishop from the eastern part of the Roman Empire

historical_references.reference: Victorinus of Aquitaine, also known as Victor of Marseille, was a Christian bishop and theologian who lived in the late 4th century AD. He was born in Aquitania, a province of the Roman Empire in present-day southwestern France, and is best known for his work 'De Antichristo', in which he identified the Antichrist as a historical figure who would come before the end times. He was also a prominent teacher and played a significant role in the development of Christian theology during the period of the early Church.
historical_references.context: Christian bishop and theologian from the western part of the Roman Empire
